newsitem.title: USA: Xerox names IBM's Richard Thoman president, COO.
newsitem.headline: Xerox names IBM's Richard Thoman president, COO.

text.p: Xerox Corp. Thursday named Richard Thoman, the number two executive at International Business Machines Corp., to the post of president and chief operating officer.
Thoman joined IBM in 1994 and was named chief financial officer in 1995. He is widely credited with turning around IBM's personal computer business.
In a statement, Xerox said Thoman will report directly to Xerox Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Paul Allaire in a newly-formed Office of the Chairman.

IBM said senior vice president and chief counsel Lawrence Ricciardi would assume Thoman's responsibilities on an interim basis. He will continue to be responsible for IBM's legal, government and intellectual property functions.
News of Thoman's departure sent shares of IBM lower in pre-market activity. IBM was singled out for pre-open selling, falling to $86 a share from $87.25.

Thoman is the second chief financial officer to leave since Louis Gerstner became Chairman of the giant computer maker. Jerome York, the previous chief financial officer, left to IBM to work for billionaire Kirk Kerkorian.
